newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on dealers covering.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on dealers covering.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended slightly higher despite uncertainty in the Tokyo market, but trading continued thin, dealers said.
Poor demand from consumers also affected bussiness which was mainly confined to short covering by dealers, they said.

"It had been a quiet day with few inquiries at the start of the week. There were some local dealers covering and business was mainly routine," a dealer said, adding that buyers continued to wait for lower prices.
Dealers said the market's rise reflected a technical correction to recent losses.
At the close, Feb RSS Ones and Feb SMR 20 buyer rose half a cent each to 304.50 cents ($1.23) and 300 cents a kg respectively.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 300 cents a kg, SMR CV at 364, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 313, SMR 10 at 301 and drum latex FOB at 237.
The market expect some demand after the Chinese Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr festivals in February when supply could be affected by fewer working days and the onset of wintering.
